report_md:
# Dollar-impulse regime: UUP 60-day impulse -> TQQQ/BIL

**Family:** `dollar regime`  
**Slug:** `family-dollar-regime`  
**Development window:** 2016-01-04 .. 2023-12-29  
**Status:** dev-only; the 2024–2026 holdout was not used.  All external frames are hard-truncated at 2023-12-29 before any feature is formed.

## 1. Hypothesis

The dollar is the price of global dollar liquidity.  When the trade-weighted dollar appreciates sharply, foreign borrowers' dollar liabilities grow, cross-border credit is squeezed, and long-duration US growth equity is vulnerable.  A flat or weaker dollar is the opposite regime: global liquidity is stable or expanding, which is a tailwind for TQQQ.

### Mechanism

The signal is deliberately a *dollar impulse*, not a QQQ trend or volatility state.  UUP tracks the ICE US Dollar Index, a broad basket dominated by EUR, JPY, GBP, CAD, SEK and CHF.  A 60-session log return above +3% is a large move (about the top quintile of the development distribution) and has historically clustered around funding stress, Fed tightening scares and risk-off episodes.  The strategy pays a small whipsaw cost for being in BIL during those episodes and stays long TQQQ otherwise.

### Why this is a distinct family

The primary object is a cross-asset currency impulse.  None of the nine existing winners uses UUP or any FX series as its gate: ratio-froth uses a QQQ/TQQQ ratio, vol-scaled-crash-stop uses realised volatility, relative-value-tqqq uses QQQ/SPY, the event families use calendar or session clocks, and the microstructure families use intraday order flow.  The dollar impulse is an external macro state, not another trend/vol/calendar variant.

## 2. Signal and execution

**External series:** UUP  
**Primary parameters:** `{'W': 60, 'THR': 0.03}`

At the close of session *k*, compute `u60 = log(UUP[k] / UUP[k-60])`.  If `u60 <= 0.030`, the target is TQQQ 1.0; otherwise it is BIL 1.0.  The feature is computed on the external daily calendar with 2015 warmup rows, then reindexed to the QQQ session calendar.  The first session already has a finite 60-day impulse.

**Execution contract.** The target for session *k* is written on the last 1-minute bar of session *k* and filled at the 09:30 open of session *k+1*.  The external close of session *k* is the latest daily print used; no bar after *k* enters the signal.  Idle capital is BIL; the book is long-only, weights ≥ 0, row sum ≤ 1, 2% rebalance band, headline 1 bp, also 5/10 bp.

## 3. Development results

### 3.1 Headline

| Book | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe | Sortino | Vol | Exposure | Fills | Turnover |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Primary, 1 bp | 41.24% | 72.11% | 0.90 | 1.24 | 55.93% | 100.0% | 131 | 682x |
| Primary, 5 bp | 40.31% | 72.24% | 0.89 | 1.23 | 55.94% | 100.0% | 131 | 660x |
| Primary, 10 bp | 39.17% | 72.41% | 0.88 | 1.21 | 55.95% | 100.0% | 131 | 633x |
| TQQQ buy & hold | 36.15% | 82.29% | 0.80 | 1.12 | 66.55% | 100.0% | 1 | 1x |
| Published dev bar | 36.72% | 82.29% | 0.82 | — | — | — | — | — |

At 1 bp the book returns 41.24% CAGR with a 72.11% max drawdown and Sharpe 0.90; at 10 bp the CAGR is still 39.17%.  TQQQ exposure is 79.9%, so the book is selectively de-risked rather than a permanent BIL overlay.

### 3.2 Activity and exposure

### 3.3 Subperiods (1 bp)

| Subperiod | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe | Sortino | Fills | TQQQ exposure |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2016-2019 | 54.69% | 53.05% | 1.19 | 1.69 | 63 | 83.4% |

## 4. Robustness

### 4.1 Eight-cell plateau

| Cell | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe | Fills | TQQQ exposure | 3-way bar |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| W=60, THR=0.02 | 36.42% | 64.33% | 0.87 | 255 | 68.3% | fail |
| W=60, THR=0.025 | 38.03% | 64.57% | 0.88 | 207 | 75.0% | PASS |
| W=60, THR=0.03 | 41.24% | 72.11% | 0.90 | 131 | 79.9% | PASS |
| W=60, THR=0.035 | 39.86% | 71.66% | 0.88 | 109 | 83.6% | PASS |
| W=60, THR=0.04 | 40.28% | 71.66% | 0.87 | 101 | 86.9% | PASS |
| W=20, THR=0.03 | 35.78% | 77.54% | 0.81 | 133 | 94.3% | fail |
| W=40, THR=0.03 | 38.08% | 71.66% | 0.84 | 153 | 86.4% | PASS |
| W=80, THR=0.03 | 45.12% | 67.27% | 0.96 | 213 | 73.6% | PASS |

**Plateau:** 6/8 cells clear the three-way dev bar (CAGR > 36.72%, DD < 82.29%, Sharpe > 0.82).

The plateau is a local cross: five thresholds at the 60-session window plus three nearby windows at the 3% threshold.  The 3.0-4.0% cells all clear the bar; the 2.0% and 2.5% cells do not.  The signal therefore has a usable plateau but is not threshold-insensitive at the low end.

### 4.2 Placebo / randomized signal dates

| Null | Mean CAGR | Median | 5th pct | 95th pct | True | Percentile | One-sided p |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Circular shift of target | 27.15% | 27.38% | 12.70% | 43.17% | 41.24% | 0.92 | 0.089 |
| Circular shift of primary feature | 27.19% | 26.42% | 12.52% | 44.84% | 41.24% | 0.90 | 0.109 |

The circular-shift nulls preserve the holding-length distribution and the marginal distribution of the dollar impulse.  The true CAGR sits near the 90th percentile of the target-shift null and near the 80th percentile of the feature-shift null.  The evidence is suggestive, not overwhelming: a 100-draw placebo on eight years of daily regimes has limited power.

### 4.3 Correlation with the nine existing winners

| Winner | Correlation | n |
|---|---:|---:|
| `relative-value-tqqq` | 0.836 | 2011 |
| `family-rebalance-flow` | 0.781 | 2011 |
| `family-ml-microstructure` | 0.764 | 2011 |
| `family-short-reversal` | 0.718 | 2011 |
| `vol-scaled-crash-stop` | 0.695 | 2011 |
| `ratio-froth` | 0.640 | 2011 |
| `family-session-timing` | 0.618 | 2011 |
| `fomc-opex-window` | 0.557 | 2011 |
| `family-intraday-microstructure-day` | 0.502 | 2011 |

Range **0.502 .. 0.836** (mean 0.679); highest with `relative-value-tqqq`.  Correlation with TQQQ itself is **0.842** (beta 0.70).

The book is still a long-TQQQ risk-on book most of the time, so it correlates with the existing risk-on winners.  The highest link is with `relative-value-tqqq`, which also rotates equity exposure; the dollar gate itself is distinct.  A correlation above 0.85 would have triggered the redundancy kill criterion.

## 5. Kill criteria

| # | Criterion | Observed | Triggered |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Activity floor: >=100 full fills or >=30 independent events | 131 fills; 65 state switches | no |
| 2 | No three-way dev improvement over TQQQ buy & hold | CAGR 41.24% vs 36.15%; DD 72.11% vs 82.29%; Sharpe 0.90 vs 0.80 | no |
| 3 | Plateau: >=5 of 8 local cells clear the three-way dev bar | 6/8 cells pass | no |
| 4 | Placebo: one-sided p <= 0.20 for at least one circular-shift null | target p=0.089; feature p=0.109 | no |
| 5 | Redundancy: maximum correlation with an existing winner <= 0.85 | 0.836 (relative-value-tqqq) | no |
| 6 | Subperiod: no negative-CAGR development subperiod | none | no |

**0 of 6 kill criteria triggered.**

## 6. Honest verdict

This is a solid dev candidate, not a verified winner.  It clears the bar and the activity floor, has a 6/8 plateau, and positive returns in all three subperiods.  The caveats are real: the edge is concentrated in 2016-19, the 2022-23 subperiod only returns 20.4%, the 2.0-2.5% threshold cells fail, and correlation with `relative-value-tqqq` is 0.836.  The one-shot holdout is the only way to know whether the dollar impulse survives.

## 7. Limitations and next steps

UUP is a fund with its own expenses and tracking error, and the daily close is a 16:00 print while the target is written at 15:59; the one-minute gap is the same convention used by the rest of the programme.  The 60-day impulse is a slow signal and can be late at turning points.  The development window contains only one major dollar cycle (2016-2023), so the threshold is not estimated on a long sample.  The next step is a frozen one-shot 2024-2026 holdout and a check of the dollar impulse against a trade-weighted Fed broad index (not just UUP) before any promotion.

## 8. Reproduction

```powershell
$env:PYTHONPATH = "C:\Users\27175\AppData\Local\Temp\opencode\pylibs"
$env:BT_THREADS = "1"
python research/new/family-dollar-regime/strategy.py
```

The script rebuilds `result.json` and this report from the development window only.
hypothesis_md:
# family-dollar-regime — hypothesis

**Status:** development-only study. The 2024–2026 holdout was not used; all external frames are hard-truncated at 2023-12-29 before any feature is formed.  
**Window:** 2016-01-04 .. 2023-12-29.  
**Primary object:** 60-session UUP log return (dollar impulse).  
**Execution:** 1-minute QQQ/TQQQ/BIL panel, signals at the session close, fills at the next 09:30 open.

## 1. Claim

A broad, persistent appreciation of the US dollar is a global tightening
shock. It raises the dollar value of foreign borrowers' liabilities, squeezes
cross-border credit, and is disproportionately negative for long-duration US
growth equity. When the dollar is flat or weakening, global liquidity is stable
or expanding and a leveraged growth-equity sleeve is supported.

The claim is directional but not symmetric. The strategy is **not** long TQQQ
because the dollar is falling; it is long TQQQ unless the dollar has just
appreciated enough to signal stress. The risk-off state is the exception, not
the base case.

## 2. Mechanism

The dollar is the funding currency of the global financial system. A large
trade-weighted appreciation tightens conditions through at least four channels:

1. **Foreign-currency debt service.** Non-US borrowers with dollar liabilities
   see their real burden rise. Credit spreads widen and dollar funding demand
   spikes.
2. **Global reserve / safe-haven demand.** Stress episodes produce a flight
   into dollars, which is itself a risk-off signal.
3. **Import prices and inflation.** A stronger dollar lowers US import prices,
   but the immediate effect on global risk assets is tighter conditions, not
   lower inflation.
4. **Earnings translation.** Large US multinationals earn abroad; a stronger
   dollar reduces translated earnings, with growth/technology names more
   sensitive to duration.

The 60-session window is long enough to distinguish a dollar *impulse* from
daily noise, but short enough to react within a quarter. The +3% threshold is a
large move: in the 2015–2023 development data, the 60-session UUP return is
above +3% in about 20% of sessions (top quintile). The strategy does not use a
QQQ 100–250 day trend, a volatility target, a drawdown event, or a calendar
clock. The only state variable is the dollar impulse.

## 3. Signal

At the close of session `k`:

```
u60[k] = log(UUP_close[k] / UUP_close[k-60])

target[k] = TQQQ 1.0   if u60[k] <= +0.030
            BIL  1.0   otherwise
```

`UUP` is the Invesco DB US Dollar Index Bullish Fund, which tracks the ICE US
Dollar Index (EUR, JPY, GBP, CAD, SEK, CHF). The external daily series starts
in 2015; the first 60-session feature for the 2016-01-04 session is therefore
finite from the first day of the development window.

The target is written on the last 1-minute bar of session `k` and filled at
the 09:30 open of session `k+1`. The external close of session `k` is the
latest daily print used. No bar after `k` enters the signal, and the external
frame is hard-truncated at 2023-12-29 before any feature is formed.

## 4. Portfolio construction and execution

- Universe: QQQ, TQQQ, BIL. The signal only uses UUP.
- Long-only, weights ≥ 0, row sum ≤ 1.
- Binary book: TQQQ 1.0 when risk-on, BIL 1.0 when risk-off. No cash drag
  beyond the BIL position.
- 2% rebalance band; fills at the next open; 1 bp headline slippage, also
  reported at 5 bp and 10 bp.
- The backtester marks the book on 1-minute QQQ/TQQQ/BIL bars. Idle capital is
  BIL, not zero-yield cash.

## 5. Primary and eight-cell plateau

The pre-registered primary is `W=60, THR=+3.0%`. The plateau is a local cross:
five thresholds at the primary window plus three nearby windows at the primary
threshold.

| Cell | W | THR | Role |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | 60 | +2.0% | tighter risk-off |
| 2 | 60 | +2.5% | tighter risk-off |
| 3 | 60 | +3.0% | **primary** |
| 4 | 60 | +3.5% | looser risk-off |
| 5 | 60 | +4.0% | looser risk-off |
| 6 | 20 | +3.0% | faster impulse |
| 7 | 40 | +3.0% | intermediate |
| 8 | 80 | +3.0% | slower impulse |

A genuine plateau should clear the three-way development bar in at least five
of the eight cells. The cells are not a search grid; they are the local
neighbourhood that a robust dollar-impulse rule should survive.

## 6. Activity floor

A publishable family must have either:

- at least 100 full fills over the development window, or
- at least 30 independent state-change events.

The dollar rule is expected to produce roughly 60–70 state changes and 120–140
fills. If it produces fewer, it is a low-activity macro overlay, not a
tradeable family, and the activity kill criterion triggers.

## 7. Kill criteria

The study is killed or demoted if any of the following is true:

| # | Criterion | Threshold |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Activity floor | fewer than 100 fills **and** fewer than 30 events |
| 2 | No three-way dev improvement | CAGR ≤ TQQQ buy-and-hold **and** DD ≥ TQQQ **and** Sharpe ≤ TQQQ |
| 3 | Plateau | fewer than 5 of 8 cells clear the three-way dev bar |
| 4 | Placebo | one-sided p > 0.20 for both circular-shift nulls |
| 5 | Redundancy | correlation > 0.85 with any of the nine existing winners |
| 6 | Subperiod instability | any of 2016–19 / 2020–21 / 2022–23 has negative CAGR |

A single triggered criterion does not automatically delete the research record,
but it does block promotion to a verified winner. Two or more triggered
criteria make the family a negative result.

## 8. Known failure modes

- **Growth-driven dollar strength.** A stronger dollar can reflect US growth
  exceptionalism and be equity-positive, not a funding shock. The 60-session
  return cannot distinguish the two.
- **Late signal.** The dollar often peaks *after* the equity drawdown has
  started. The strategy can be long TQQQ into the first leg of a crash (2020)
  and only de-risk after the dollar has already moved.
- **UUP basket composition.** UUP is heavily EUR/JPY; a broad trade-weighted
  dollar index would be a better object. The result is conditional on the UUP
  basket.
- **One dollar cycle.** The development window contains one major dollar cycle
  (2016–2023). The +3% threshold is not estimated on a long sample.
- **Overlap with risk-on winners.** The book is long TQQQ ~80% of the time, so
  its return stream correlates with existing risk-on families even if the gate
  is distinct.

## 9. Why this is a distinct family

The primary object is a cross-asset currency impulse. None of the nine
existing winners uses UUP or any FX series as its gate:

- `ratio-froth` uses a QQQ/TQQQ ratio.
- `vol-scaled-crash-stop` uses realised volatility and a crash stop.
- `relative-value-tqqq` uses QQQ/SPY relative value.
- `fomc-opex-window` uses a calendar event window.
- `family-session-timing` uses intraday session blocks.
- `family-short-reversal` uses 1–5 day price overreaction.
- `family-rebalance-flow` uses mechanical LETF/closing flow.
- `family-intraday-microstructure-day` uses opening range/order flow.
- `family-ml-microstructure` uses a fitted ML model on intraday features.

The dollar impulse is an external macro state. It is not a QQQ trend, a
volatility target, a drawdown event, a calendar clock, an opening-range rule, a
relative-strength ratio gate, or an ML model.

## 10. Data and reproducibility

- External: `data/external/UUP.parquet` (Yahoo adjusted close, 2015–2026;
  only rows ≤ 2023-12-29 are used).
- Execution: local `data/intraday-hf/QQQ-1m.parquet`, `TQQQ-1m.parquet`,
  `BIL-1m.parquet`.
- Warmup: external 2015 rows are used only to make the first 60-session
  feature finite on 2016-01-04.
- Run: `python research/new/family-dollar-regime/strategy.py`.
- The script writes `result.json` and `report.md` from the development window
  only.

## 11. Decision rule

If the primary clears the three-way bar, the activity floor, at least 5/8
plateau cells, and at least one placebo null at p ≤ 0.20, and no subperiod is
negative, it is a **dev candidate** eligible for a frozen one-shot holdout. It
is not a verified winner until that holdout and the causality/freshness audit
are complete.

If the primary fails the bar or the plateau, it remains a negative research
record. A high headline CAGR with a fragile plateau is not a winner.

"""Dollar-impulse regime sleeve - `family-dollar-regime`.

DEVELOPMENT WINDOW ONLY (2016-01-04 .. 2023-12-29).  The 2024-2026 holdout is
never loaded.

Primary object: the 60-session log return of UUP, the PowerShares DB US Dollar
Index Bullish Fund.  A broad dollar appreciation of more than 3% over 60
sessions is treated as a global dollar-funding / tightening shock and the book
moves to BIL.  Otherwise the book holds TQQQ.  The signal is a dollar impulse,
not a QQQ price-trend, volatility or calendar gate.

Rules (all known at the session-k close; fill at the next open):

    u60[k] = log(UUP_close[k] / UUP_close[k-60])
    target[k] = TQQQ 1.0 if u60[k] <= +0.030 else BIL 1.0

The target is written on the last 1-minute bar of session k and filled at the
09:30 open of k+1.  Long-only, weights >= 0, row sum <= 1, 2% band, headline
1 bp, also 5/10 bp.  Idle capital is BIL.

Run:
    $env:PYTHONPATH = "C:\\Users\\27175\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\opencode\\pylibs"
    $env:BT_THREADS = "1"
    python research/new/family-dollar-regime/strategy.py
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parents[2]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "research" / "new"))
import ext_family_common as common  # noqa: E402
import external  # noqa: E402

SLUG = "family-dollar-regime"
SYMBOLS = ["UUP"]
PARAMS = dict(W=60, THR=0.03)

# Eight local cells: five thresholds at the primary window plus three nearby
# windows at the primary threshold.  The primary (60, 0.03) is included.
PLATEAU = (
    [dict(W=60, THR=x) for x in (0.020, 0.025, 0.030, 0.035, 0.040)]
    + [dict(W=w, THR=0.03) for w in (20, 40, 80)]
)


def signal(px: pd.DataFrame, idx: pd.DatetimeIndex, params: dict) -> pd.Series:
    """60-session UUP log impulse, sliced to the QQQ session calendar."""
    s = np.log(px["UUP"] / px["UUP"].shift(int(params["W"])))
    return common.session_slice(s, idx)


def targets_from_signal(sig: pd.Series, params: dict) -> np.ndarray:
    """TQQQ when the dollar impulse is at or below the threshold, else BIL."""
    on = (sig <= float(params["THR"])).fillna(False).to_numpy()
    return common.binary_targets(on)


def build_weights_p(ts, opens, closes, params=None, px=None):
    p = dict(PARAMS)
    if params:
        p.update(params)
    if px is None:
        px = common.daily_panel(ts, SYMBOLS)
    idx = external.session_index(ts)
    sig = signal(px, idx, p)
    t = targets_from_signal(sig, p)
    w = external.daily_targets_to_weights(ts, t)
    if w.min() < -1e-12 or w.sum(axis=1).max() > 1.0 + 1e-9:
        raise AssertionError("invalid weights")
    return w


def build_weights(ts, opens, closes):
    """Return the (n, 3) long-only weight matrix for the pre-registered primary."""
    return build_weights_p(ts, opens, closes, PARAMS)


def _passes(s: dict) -> bool:
    return bool(s["cagr"] > common.BAR["cagr"]
                and s["max_drawdown"] < common.BAR["max_drawdown"]
                and s["sharpe"] > common.BAR["sharpe"])


def _beats_bench(s: dict, bench: dict) -> bool:
    return bool(s["cagr"] > bench["cagr"]
                and s["max_drawdown"] < bench["max_drawdown"]
                and s["sharpe"] > bench["sharpe"])


def main():
    ts, o, c = common.load_panel()
    px = common.daily_panel(ts, SYMBOLS)
    idx = external.session_index(ts)
    sig = signal(px, idx, PARAMS)
    targets = targets_from_signal(sig, PARAMS)
    w = external.daily_targets_to_weights(ts, targets)

    windows = {}
    res1 = eqd1 = None
    for bp in common.SLIPS:
        s, res, eqd = common.stats_block(ts, o, c, w, bp)
        windows[f"{bp:g}bp"] = s
        if bp == 1.0:
            res1, eqd1 = res, eqd

    act = common.activity(targets)
    act["fills"] = windows["1bp"]["fills"]
    act["activity_floor_pass"] = bool(
        act["fills"] >= 100 or act["independent_events"] >= 30)

    bench = common.benchmark_block(ts, o, c)
    sub = common.subperiod_block(ts, o, c, w)
    yearly = common.yearly_table(ts, c, eqd1)
    corr = common.correlation_block(ts, c, eqd1)

    plateau = []
    for p in PLATEAU:
        wp = build_weights_p(ts, o, c, p, px=px)
        sp, _, _ = common.stats_block(ts, o, c, wp, 1.0)
        plateau.append({
            "params": p,
            "cagr": sp["cagr"],
            "max_drawdown": sp["max_drawdown"],
            "sharpe": sp["sharpe"],
            "sortino": sp["sortino"],
            "fills": sp["fills"],
            "turnover": sp["turnover"],
            "tqqq_exposure": sp["tqqq_exposure"],
            "passes_bar": _passes(sp),
        })

    placebo = common.placebo_block(
        ts, o, c, targets, sig.to_numpy(),
        lambda x: targets_from_signal(pd.Series(x, index=idx), PARAMS),
        n=100,
    )

    w1 = windows["1bp"]
    plateau_pass = sum(1 for x in plateau if x["passes_bar"])
    neg_sub = {k: v["cagr"] for k, v in sub.items() if v["cagr"] < 0}
    p_t = placebo["shift_target"]["p_one_sided"]
    p_f = placebo["shift_feature"]["p_one_sided"]

    kills = [
        {"rule": "Activity floor: >=100 full fills or >=30 independent events",
         "observed": f"{act['fills']} fills; {act['independent_events']} state switches",
         "triggered": not act["activity_floor_pass"]},
        {"rule": "No three-way dev improvement over TQQQ buy & hold",
